name: Finite State Machine for Interpolant Modelling
definition: A representation of isosurface evolution by sweeping from high to low isovalues. States are cases; transitions occur when a vertex changes from white to black. Used to impose constraints on possible configurations.
summary: The Finite State Machine for Interpolant Modelling maps Marching Cubes case transitions during isovalue sweeps to enforce topological constraints, distinguishing itself by validating interpolant paths rather than relying on static lookup tables.
